description:
FILED s408 (Opus 5) while shipping #337 (the my-sub scope rename).

perl lets a LEXICAL SUB take a keyword's name, and t/op/lexsub.t asserts it:

    { our   sub if() { 42 }  my $x = if if if;  is $x, 42 }   # line 71
    { state sub if() { 44 }  my $x = if if if;  is $x, 44 }   # line 209
    { my    sub if() { 44 }  my $x = if if if;  is $x, 44 }   # line 576

Three zero-arg calls juxtaposed.  PCL has TWO distinct problems here, and #337
converted four instances of the worse one into four instances of the milder:

(a) NOT RENAMED (`our sub if`, a package sub by design): the statement is still
    read by the KEYWORD parser and emits

        (p-if (p-if) (p-my-= $x (p-if)))

    a zero-argument p-if.  Its macroexpansion error IS t/op/lexsub.t's crash
    ("Form: (p-if) Compile-time error: during macroexp"), which is why that
    file stops at 6 of 156 rows.  A statement-modifier `if` with NO condition
    should never be emitted -- this is a rule-12 case in the statement lowerer:
    the missing case must say so, not build a form that cannot expand.

(b) RENAMED (`my`/`state sub if`, #337): the statement becomes
    `my $x = if__lexsub__6 if__lexsub__6 if__lexsub__6;` -- three juxtaposed
    zero-arg calls, which the TERM GRAMMAR cannot lower
    ("Bug. Fell through. Missing case: ["), so it is an announced DROP.
    Census edited s408: t/op/lexsub.t 6 -> 10, with the trade argued in the
    census header.

FIX SHAPE: (b) is Option B phase 2's term-grammar track (docs/option-b-phase2-plan.md,
#372's family) -- `TERM TERM TERM` where each is a declared empty-prototype
sub.  Do NOT special-case it in the $end_pars region.  (a) is independent and
cheap-ish: find where a statement-modifier `if` with an empty condition is
built and make it DIE naming the shape (rule 12), which would also stop
t/op/lexsub.t crashing and let its remaining ~150 rows be measured for the
first time -- size THAT before (b), since it is what gates the file.

MEASURE FIRST: how many rows does t/op/lexsub.t produce once (a) no longer
crashes it?  The s396 lesson -- "one refusal blocks N rows" is an upper bound
until the file has run.  Related: #341 (op/lexsub.t sizing), #337 (done).


HALF (a) DONE s408 (Opus 5) -- the zero-argument (p-if) is GONE.

CAUSE, which the task guessed at: `if` is in ExprToCL's %RUNTIME_NAMES, so a
bareword `if` reaching the funcall generator lowered to the p-if MACRO with
whatever arity it happened to have.  A statement keyword is never a FUNCTION,
so the generator now refuses it and the statement becomes a counted, announced
DROP -- the #138 family -- instead of a form whose macroexpansion kills the
file.

REUSE (the USER asked, mid-session, whether something already checked this):
there was no predicate -- the same six modifier words were INLINED as a regex
in four parser sites, and the two NAMED sets nearby answer different questions
(%SIG_DEFAULT_KEYWORDS = does a bareword make a signature default swallow;
InterpScan %KEYWORDS = perl's whole keyword list, builtins included, for the
interpolation weigher).  So Pl::PExpr::Config now holds BOTH sets --
statement_modifiers (the six that can trail an expression) and
statement_keywords (those plus else/elsif) -- and the four inline copies were
converged onto is_statement_modifier().

MEASURED: op/lexsub.t 6/8 -> 7/10 (its next blocker is a different one,
undef-fn:main::pl-F); census t/op/lexsub.t 10 -> 14 with the trade argued;
corpus-diff IDENTICAL 111; emission-ab over perl's own t/ 559 SAME / 1 DIFF
(that file alone); gate 149/5439.  Guard rows in Pl/t/lexical-sub-01.t.

HALF (b) REMAINS: `TERM TERM TERM` of declared empty-prototype subs is Option B
phase 2's term grammar (#372 family).  The renamed spelling (`my`/`state sub
if`) drops there today; only the unrenamed `our sub if` went through (a).

HALF (b) CORRECTED s409 (Fable review): it is NOT "TERM TERM TERM of
empty-prototype subs".  Deparsed under perl 5.40.3:

    { state sub if () { 44 }  my $x = if if if; print $x }
      ->  my $x = 44;      i.e.  (my $x = if()) if if()

The FIRST and THIRD `if` are in TERM position (a call to the lexical); the
MIDDLE one is in OPERATOR position and stays the statement-MODIFIER keyword.
(perl also makes a following `if (1) {...}` STATEMENT fail -- "Too many
arguments for if" -- because statement start is a term position too; so a
keyword-named lexical sub genuinely takes over term-position `if`s.)  #337's
renamer rewrites ALL THREE, which is what makes the statement unparseable ->
the drop.  The correct rewrite is POSITION-AWARE: rename a keyword-named
lexical sub only where a TERM is expected (the operator-vs-term question the
token repairs already answer -- Parser2::_is_method_name_word's family), leave
the operator-position occurrence as the keyword.  Alternatively EXCLUDE
statement keywords from the rename entirely (the keyword parse then hits half
(a)'s counted drop -- same count, no hazard).  Exotic (t/op/lexsub.t only,
three statements); stays behind Option B phase 2 as ruled (fable-answers-s408
§3.6) -- whichever session touches it, the fix is in the RENAMER's
classification, not in the term grammar.


HALF (b) DONE s430 (Fable) -- B3.3 of docs/b3-operand-collapse-s428.md.  The fix is in the RENAMER, as s409 said: _rename_lexical_subs is POSITION-AWARE for the six statement-modifier names (Pl::PExpr::Config::is_statement_modifier) -- a use is rewritten only where perl would look the bareword up as a lexical sub (toke.c: PL_expect != XOPERATOR), i.e. NOT after a token that ends a term (_ends_term, the repairs oracle, which gained the postfix ++/-- arm), a bareword term (_word_is_term), or a `()` call the pass itself just produced.  `our sub if` is the same rule with the qualified spelling `main::if` for term-position uses (perl aliases the lexical `if` to &main::if; the declaration stays `our sub if`).  PPI structure built around the keyword is re-classed in place (_reclass_keyword_call_site): a statement-initial Compound (`if;`, `map { if }`, `(unless, 2)`), the orphan sibling PPI split off (`(for, for)`), and the Condition after `if()`.  Probes identical to perl across 40+ shapes (my/state/our x same/other package, `if()`, `&if`, `\&if`, `defined &if`, `if;`, `(unless, 2)`, `3 + unless`, `unless unless 0`, `$t += for for 1..2`, `(for, for)`, `$i++ while`, `"@{[ unless ]}"`).  Guard Pl/t/lexical-sub-02.t (6 rows) + lexical-sub-01.t rows 20-22 rewritten from the DROP they asserted to the lowering.  op/lexsub.t census 12 -> 4; corpus-diff IDENTICAL; lib/cpan A/B SAME; perl-t A/B 603/604 (only lexsub.t).  Not B3.3: the `x` lexsub drops (lines 448/751/836/851, PPI lexes a sub named x as the operator) stay -- #376/#361 family.
subject: A lexical sub named after a KEYWORD (`state sub if() {44}; my $x = if if if`): the unrenamed half emits a zero-arg (p-if) that crashes op/lexsub.t; the renamed half is a term-grammar drop
